issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the animal feeding method: the UML and solution use the abstract method name messageOnFeed(), while other places in the problem statement refer to getFeedingSound(). Specifically, the UML in the problem statement declares abstract messageOnFeed() (problem_statement.md line 28) and the solution's Animal.java declares public abstract String messageOnFeed() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java line 18). However, the problem text instructs that Seal/Pig/Goat implement getFeedingSound() with specific return values (problem_statement.md line 97) and later says feedAllAnimals() calls getFeedingSound() on all animals (problem_statement.md line 110). The solution's Farm.feedAllAnimals implementation calls messageOnFeed() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 27-31). This mismatch can lead students to implement the wrong method name (getFeedingSound vs messageOnFeed), causing compilation errors or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the feeding method name consistent across all artifacts. Prefer using messageOnFeed() (matches the UML and the reference solution): update all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem statement and template comments to messageOnFeed(), and update the example text and the feedAllAnimals description to call messageOnFeed(). Alternatively, if you prefer getFeedingSound(), rename the abstract method and all references in the solution and tests accordingly. Ensure the chosen name is used uniformly in UML, problem text, template comments, and solution code so students implement the correct method and avoid compilation/test failures.

issues.description: The exercise refers to the animal feeding-sound method using two different identifiers. The UML and reference code define an abstract method named messageOnFeed() on Animal and implement it in Seal, Pig, and Goat (Animal.messageOnFeed(), Seal.messageOnFeed(), Pig.messageOnFeed(), Goat.messageOnFeed()). However, the problem statement text also uses getFeedingSound() when describing expected return values and when explaining feedAllAnimals(), e.g. 'getFeedingSound() should return ...' and 'feedAllAnimals() calls getFeedingSound()'. Students may be unsure whether to implement messageOnFeed() or getFeedingSound(), and whether feedAllAnimals() should call one or the other.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the feeding-sound method. Preferred fix: update problem_statement.md to replace the occurrences of getFeedingSound() (lines noted above) with messageOnFeed() so the description matches the UML and the provided code (Animal.messageOnFeed() and its overrides). Alternatively, if you prefer the name getFeedingSound(), rename the abstract method and all overrides/uses (Animal.messageOnFeed -> Animal.getFeedingSound, and update Farm and all subclasses accordingly) across all source files and the UML so all artifacts consistently use the same name.
